$comment: Config for scripts/check-pr-review-signal.mjs (issue #3312).
This file lives under scripts/, and .github/workflows/pr-review-signal.yml carries NO
path filter, so the job that reads it fires on every pull_request event regardless of
which files changed. That is deliberate: #3305's gate could not fire on the file it
guarded because that file was in no path filter, and a presence check that can itself be
filtered out is the same defect.
`reviewers` are the check CONTEXTS whose descriptions are adjudicated. Adding an
unrelated context here would make this gate opine on free text it has no business
reading; keep it to bot reviewers that claim a verdict on the code.
`phrases` are matched as case-insensitive PREFIXES of the description, and only against
a `success` state. `neutral` and `failure` already communicate 'no verdict'.
`excludeJobKeys` drops `test` -- the `Build + WASM + Rust + Node` aggregate. It is
`needs:` twelve jobs and publishes NO check run until every one of them finishes, so
waiting for it means waiting out the whole matrix. Measured by `created_at` -- when a
lane becomes PRESENT, which is what this gate polls for, not `started_at` -- from each
run's own creation, over the 68 completed test.yml PR runs of 2026-08-25/26 that
published it: the aggregate appeared at min 509, median 894, max 2067 seconds, with 33
of the 68 past the 900 s budget. The last NON-aggregate lane appeared at min 161,
median 190, p95 522, max 845 seconds: 0 of the 68 past it. Requiring the aggregate makes
the wait a function of the SUITE's total runtime, which grows, and would false-fail half
of every green PR; requiring only the lanes makes it a function of how fast GitHub
creates check runs. Nothing is lost: the aggregate is one of only two contexts in main's ruleset, so
branch protection already blocks on it, and the #3294 total-absence shape still fails
here naming all fifteen lanes. Asserted in check-pr-review-signal.test.mjs.
`reviewVerdictSeverity` is `warn`, and that is a considered downgrade rather than a
retreat -- see the note on the key itself.

phrases.means: the reviewer hit its quota and read none of this diff
the reviewer declined to run at all
the reviewer was out of quota
the reviewer was out of quota

$reviewVerdictSeverityComment: WARN, NOT FAIL, AND THE EVIDENCE IS THAT A RATE-LIMITED STATUS NEVER SELF-HEALS.
The full status history on such a SHA is `queued -> in progress -> success/Review rate
limited`, and then nothing, forever. The quota recovers; the status on that commit does
not. So `fail` means red until a human pushes a commit or triggers an on-demand review --
on 8 of the 19 open PRs measured the day this shipped. That is exactly the class this repo
already ruled on when it marked check-coderabbit-review.mjs and check-pr-green.mjs
`@unwired-by-design`: 'a required check built on transient GitHub state fails for reasons
unrelated to the diff under test'. The finding is still printed and still quotes the
reviewer verbatim, so nothing is hidden -- it just does not hold the PR red on a quota.
The LANE half has no knob and cannot be downgraded: a missing test lane is a fact about
